# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 21 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Thanksgiving Hymns Column 21 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 21:5 — "created" vs. "made" — verb choice for divine formation of the righteous

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "You, You alone have created the-righteous-one" | Emphatic pronoun doubling reflects Hebrew attah attah; hyphenated construct |
| LOGOS | "You alone have created the righteous one" | Single pronoun sufficient; English emphasis through "alone" |
| PNEUMA | "You alone made the righteous person" | "Made" is more natural English than "created" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The emphatic "You alone" captures the Hebrew emphasis without awkward doubling. "Created" (bara') preferred over "made" since the passage concerns origination, not craftsmanship.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:8 — "above the flesh" vs. "above mortal flesh" vs. "beyond mere human existence"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "above the-flesh" | Literal basar with article |
| LOGOS | "above mortal flesh" | Adds "mortal" to clarify the contrastive sense |
| PNEUMA | "beyond mere human existence" | Full paraphrase for modern accessibility |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Mortal flesh" captures the theological contrast without PNEUMA's excessive expansion or EMET's bare literalism.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:9 — "consecrated" vs. "set apart" vs. "marked" — dedication of the wicked for destruction

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "You consecrated them" | Literal hqdshtm — root qdsh used even for negative consecration |
| LOGOS | "You set them apart" | Avoids positive connotation of "consecrated" for wicked persons |
| PNEUMA | "You marked them" | Dynamic equivalent avoiding religious register entirely |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Set apart" preserves the separating action of the Hebrew root qdsh without the positive cultic overtones that "consecrated" carries in English.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:13-14 — "spirit of flesh" — key sectarian anthropological term

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "spirit-of flesh" | Hyphenated construct chain ruach basar |
| LOGOS | "spirit of flesh" | Preserves sectarian term without hyphenation |
| PNEUMA | "mere mortal" | Dynamic equivalent for modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Spirit of flesh" (ruach basar) is a core Hodayot anthropological concept distinguishing human creaturely weakness from divine spirit. PNEUMA's "mere mortal" loses this crucial theological dimension.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Sectarian terminology must be preserved.

---

## 21:16 — "construction of dust" vs. "thing fashioned of dust" vs. "shaped from dirt"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a construction-of dust" | Literal yetser 'afar |
| LOGOS | "a thing fashioned of dust" | More natural English while preserving the formation metaphor |
| PNEUMA | "merely shaped from dirt" | Contemporary register; "dirt" for 'afar |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Thing fashioned of dust" is dignified enough for theological discourse while remaining clear. "Dirt" (PNEUMA) is too colloquial; "construction" (EMET) is awkward in English.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:17 — "spirit of crookedness" vs. "perverse spirit" vs. "twisted spirit"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a spirit-of crookedness rules over him" | Literal ruach 'awlah |
| LOGOS | "a perverse spirit holds dominion over him" | "Perverse" standard DSS translation; "holds dominion" for mshl |
| PNEUMA | "driven by a twisted spirit" | Dynamic restructuring |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Perverse spirit" is the recognized scholarly rendering. "Holds dominion" better captures the Hebrew mshl than EMET's "rules."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:23 — "angels of holiness" vs. "holy angels" vs. "the holy angels"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "angels-of holiness" | Literal mal'akhei qodesh as construct chain |
| LOGOS | "holy angels" | Standard English adjectival form |
| PNEUMA | "the holy angels" | Added article for naturalness |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Holy angels" is natural English and the standard DSS rendering. EMET's construct form is unnecessarily Hebraizing; PNEUMA's added article is acceptable but unnecessary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:32 — "no price" vs. "beyond all reckoning" vs. "priceless beyond measure"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to Your might there is no price" | Literal mechir with negation |
| LOGOS | "Your might is beyond all reckoning" | Formal English idiom conveying immeasurability |
| PNEUMA | "Your power is priceless beyond measure" | Intensified for rhetorical impact |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Beyond all reckoning" aptly conveys the Hebrew sense of immeasurability in dignified English. EMET's "no price" is ambiguous; PNEUMA's "priceless beyond measure" is redundant.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
